title: Skill Up I Développement Et Modélisation D'Un Vêtement Fini
description:
Envie de réaliser une veste bomber à partir d’un bloc de base masculin, développé et rendu entièrement sur CLO ? Rejoignez notre prochain Skill Up workshop en ligne afin d'explorer chaque étape du processus de conception, depuis l'altération du patron de base jusqu’à l’obtention d’un produit fini, prêt à être rendu et industrialisé.⁠
⁠
Faisant suite au précédent Skill-UP en français, cette session constitue la continuation logique du programme. Elle vous permettra d’approfondir votre compréhension du processus de développement produit et de perfectionner votre utilisation des outils essentiels à chaque étape sur CLO.⁠

markdown_content: ## Overview: Webinar Goal, Versions, and Demo Setup This section sets the context for the “Skill Up” session: importing training files into Clo, using the base avatar *Thomas* (default size), and building a men’s bomber pattern. It also specifies the Clo version recommendation and where participants can ask questions. - Training files must be transmitted to participants and are available in **Demio**. - Workflow: **download → decompress → link files** into Clo before starting. - The demo is built on the **basic avatar: Thomas** in his **basic size**. - Pose used: **Nv2 Naro**. - Clo version: - Recommended: **2025.1.240** - Suggested minimum for compatibility: **2025.0** (to ensure interface/function compatibility). - Duration: presentation ~**1 hour**, then a short exchange/Q&A. ## Importing Training Files and Preparing the Workspace This section explains how to open the Clo library, create/link a new library from the decompressed training archive, and add the provided garment elements to the workspace. 1. Open the **library** from the **top-right icon**. 2. Create a **new library** if needed, to link the training file. 3. Link the decompressed archive, specifically the file named **“SkillFiles”**. 4. After linking, the training contents appear in the library and can be added to the workspace by: - **double-click**, or - **right-click → “Add to the workspace.”** 5. The relevant garment elements are found in **“Trim & Fabrice”** (used later for garment construction and materials). ## Avatar Considerations: Activate Joint Spacing (If Needed) This section covers a common avatar-related adjustment when working with a fitted avatar mesh and close arm positions. - The demo uses: - **basic model**: *Thomas* - **default size** - pose: **Nv2 Naro** - The avatar arms may be **slightly closer to the body**, which can cause issues for some pieces. - If needed: - **activate avatar joints** - select a joint and add **small spacing** between avatar body parts to avoid collisions. ## Building the Bomber From a Men’s Base Block This section walks through starting from a men’s base block and transforming it into a bomber by editing pattern volumes from largest to smallest (front/back first, then sleeve and collar). - Start from the existing base patterns: - **men’s block** - **men’s sleeve** - **collar** (modified slightly) - Goal: reach a **bomber** construction similar to what’s used in promotional contexts for the webinar. ### Pattern editing strategy (volume, then details) - Work **from largest to smallest**. - Adjust the **pattern volume** first, then refine piece boundaries. ## Front/Back Volume Reduction Using Pattern Modification (mm and 60 mm Example) This section describes reducing the overall pattern width by using box-based selection and guides, then entering numeric values (in **millimeters**). 1. Use the **Modify Pattern** tool. 2. Select the **bottom of the front** and create a **box angle back** selection for guidance. 3. Select the **bottom of the back**. 4. Use **Shift** to obtain **guides** and prevent unwanted deviation while moving upward. 5. Use **right-click** to open a menu and enter the numeric value for narrowing. 6. Example value used: - Narrowing amount: **60 millimeters** (user notes they are working in **mm**). ## Creating Bomber Front Hook/Edge and Adjusting Width (7 cm → 5 cm) This section explains how to create and refine the first bomber front piece boundary, including entering exact distances via right-click. - With the same **Modify Pattern** tool: - left-click and drag a corner/edge into the desired position (magnetic/guided behavior due to prior points). - After placement, select the relevant line to read displayed distances (example: **7 cm**). - To reduce to **5 cm**: 1. left-click on the line and slide it, 2. right-click to enter the travel/distance value. - Example entered: - **20 millimeters** to achieve the desired **5 mm/cm-level** adjustment on the selected front hook area (as demonstrated). ## Back Construction: Internal Line Creation, Cut, and Borderline Separation This section covers generating an internal line on the back, cutting along it, and preparing front/back borderlines for further editing. - Back differs from front, so the back is handled with: - creation of an **internal line** based on a chosen point (example reference: “point at 5”). - Internal line creation method shown: 1. left-click once on the starting point, 2. double left-click to validate (line traces on both sides due to symmetry line). - Cut along the internal line: - select the line → right-click → choose **Cut** to separate into two pieces. - Result: - back borderline is established, while an extra piece remains (handled later). ## Front Borderline Creation: Rectangle in 2D and Symmetry Workflow This section describes creating the front borderline using a measured rectangle and working efficiently **in half** using symmetry links. - Check measurements (example shown around **260** out of **5** in the interface context). - Use **multi-rectangle in 2D** to create the rectangle that fits. - To work efficiently: - add **symmetry links** so actions on one side mirror the other. - Front processing steps: 1. Add an internal line at the **front middle**. 2. Cut to separate front/back into distinct pieces. 3. Delete the side that isn’t needed (example: delete right side). 4. Work only on the remaining side (left). ### Merge borderlines after half-work - Use **Modify Pattern** tool: - select two lines (left-click + **Shift** + second left-click), - right-click one selected line → **Merge**. - Merge creates: - blue merge baseline behavior, - points at merge-line level to keep values consistent. ## Applying Elasticity Reduction: 80% Width on Borderline Pieces This section explains reducing the pattern width via the pattern transformation tool, then mirroring symmetrically so both sides match. - Select the borderline piece(s) and use **pattern transformation**. - The transformation box provides circles to adjust: - proportionally, or - only **height**, or only **width**. - The demo keeps height correct (example: **5 cm height**) and reduces width: - reduce to **80%** global width (removing 20% of full width). - After narrowing left side: - apply symmetrical modification (right-click → symmetry with couture) to recreate the right side with the same **80%** reduction. ## Sleeve Borderline Reduction and Duplication to the Other Side This section applies the same reduction logic to the sleeve, then duplicates the sleeve pattern to the opposite side using symmetry with seam. - Sleeve values: - example height shown: **296.8** - target height: **50 millimeters** - Apply reduction: - set reduction to **80%** - validate. - Duplicate to right sleeve: - use **clone with symmetry and seam**. - shortcuts mentioned: **Ctrl+C** and **Ctrl+B** (or right-click clone options). ## Increasing Double Thickness for Bomber Hem/Edge (Contour Compensation at 50 mm) This section shows compensating pattern contour around pleat/edge areas to achieve the needed “double thickness” behavior for the bomber. - Objective: create the **double thickness** desired for this type of product. - Method: contour compensation at the pleat/edge line. - Steps: 1. select the line where pleats/edge duplication occurs, 2. enlarge (not retract), 3. enter distance **50 millimeters** (global height), 4. enable an option to create an **internal line** to support later pleat arrangement tools. - Apply the same operation to: - back and front hem/borderline pieces. ## Collar Construction: Polygon Curve on Front Center and Cutting This section explains constructing a curved collar shape using a polygon tool in 2D, then cutting using an internal line and troubleshooting internal-line-to-outline issues. - Collar height target: **5 centimeters**. - Bomber collar behavior: - often returns to **zero at front center** - rises to about **3.5 cm, 5 cm, or more** at the back/waist center level (as stated). - Steps: 1. Use **polygon tool** with **internal line** in 2D. 2. Start at **front center** (internal line reference). 3. left-click to mark curve start, 4. left-click to define points; for curves, drag to create handles (curve editing via mouse). 5. Validate with a second click or **double-click** at the end. - After curve creation: - select the internal line and **cut** it. - Caveat: - if the internal line doesn’t meet the pattern outline, cutting can fail. - fix by extending the internal line to the outline or adjusting the pattern. ## Collar Double Thickness: Layer Clone Below (Green Visual, Sewn to Source) This section explains how to create collar thickness

Cut along the internal line: - select the line → right-click → choose **Cut** to separate into two pieces. - Result: - back borderline is established, while an extra piece remains (handled later). ## Front Borderline Creation: Rectangle in 2D and Symmetry Workflow This section describes creating the front borderline using a measured rectangle and working efficiently **in half** using symmetry links. - Check measurements (example shown around **260** out of **5** in the interface context). - Use **multi-rectangle in 2D** to create the rectangle that fits. - To work efficiently: - add **symmetry links** so actions on one side mirror the other. - Front processing steps: 1. Add an internal line at the **front middle**. 2. Cut to separate front/back into distinct pieces. 3. Delete the side that isn’t needed (example: delete right side). 4. Work only on the remaining side (left). ### Merge borderlines after half-work - Use **Modify Pattern** tool: - select two lines (left-click + **Shift** + second left-click), - right-click one selected line → **Merge**. - Merge creates: - blue merge baseline behavior, - points at merge-line level to keep values consistent.

Select the borderline piece(s) and use **pattern transformation**. - The transformation box provides circles to adjust: - proportionally, or - only **height**, or only **width**. - The demo keeps height correct (example: **5 cm height**) and reduces width: - reduce to **80%** global width (removing 20% of full width). - After narrowing left side: - apply symmetrical modification (right-click → symmetry with couture) to recreate the right side with the same **80%** reduction. ## Sleeve Borderline Reduction and Duplication to the Other Side This section applies the same reduction logic to the sleeve, then duplicates the sleeve pattern to the opposite side using symmetry with seam. - Sleeve values: - example height shown: **296.8** - target height: **50 millimeters** - Apply reduction: - set reduction to **80%** - validate. - Duplicate to right sleeve: - use **clone with symmetry and seam**. - shortcuts mentioned: **Ctrl+C** and **Ctrl+B** (or right-click clone options). ## Increasing Double Thickness for Bomber Hem/Edge (Contour Compensation at 50 mm) This section shows compensating pattern contour around pleat/edge areas to achieve the needed “double thickness” behavior for the bomber. - Objective: create the **double thickness** desired for this type of product. - Method: contour compensation at the pleat/edge line. - Steps: 1. select the line where pleats/edge duplication occurs, 2. enlarge (not retract), 3. enter distance **50 millimeters** (global height), 4. enable an option to create an **internal line** to support later pleat arrangement tools. - Apply the same operation to: - back and front hem/borderline pieces. ## Collar Construction: Polygon Curve on Front Center and Cutting This section explains constructing a curved collar shape using a polygon tool in 2D, then cutting using an internal line and troubleshooting internal-line-to-outline issues. - Collar height target: **5 centimeters**. - Bomber collar behavior: - often returns to **zero at front center** - rises to about **3.5 cm, 5 cm, or more** at the back/waist center level (as stated). - Steps: 1. Use **polygon tool** with **internal line** in 2D. 2. Start at **front center** (internal line reference). 3. left-click to mark curve start, 4. left-click to define points; for curves, drag to create handles (curve editing via mouse). 5. Validate with a second click or **double-click** at the end. - After curve creation: - select the internal line and **cut** it.
